content.text:
The barista asks if you’ll have your drink here. Answer: 포장해 주세요. — “To go, please.” Say it once, then try again in 3 minutes.

Want another café turn? Language Cafe’s free Korean café mission lets you order a drink and answer the next question. Log in to start; no card required.

Try it → https://languagestudio.uk/missions/korean-cafe/?utm_source=threads&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=language_cafe&utm_content=takeaway-reply-20260925

images.altText: At a warm café counter, the mint mascot gestures toward a takeaway cup and bag. The card teaches 포장해 주세요. as “To go, please.”
A cup points toward a takeaway bag on a mint card; 포장해 주세요. means “To go, please.”
Two speech bubbles show a café exchange: staff asks 매장에서 드시나요? and customer answers 포장해 주세요.
A drink moves from the counter toward a takeaway bag; use 포장해 주세요. when you want the ordered drink to go.
A latte order and the prompt “For here?” leave a blank space for the learner to say the Korean takeaway answer aloud.
A three-minute recall path leads to a separate free Korean café mission; the direct link appears in the Threads caption.

koreanExpressionAccuracy.evidence: The polite line 포장해 주세요. naturally answers 매장에서 드시나요? for a takeaway café order.

englishExplanation.evidence: To go, please. is a natural short English bridge for this exact polite Korean request.

mobileLegibility.evidence: All six 1080x1350 cards and the 270-pixel phone contact sheet were visually checked; main copy and Hangul remain legible without clipping.

siteOfferAccuracy.evidence: The live Korean café mission is free, asks for login but no card, and has a café-order follow-up; the cards do not promise this exact expression is taught there.

draftEvidence.notes: The live mission offer, expression and artwork were reviewed. This job alone does not authorize publication without its separate matching grant.
